summary: Pours based purely on the spout's own tilt, so anything can drive the can.
overview: Pouring is derived from how far the SPOUT has tilted away from the orientation it started in — there is no "is pouring" flag to wire and no assumption about what rotates the can. A mouse drag, a VR grip or an animation can all drive the same transform and this just works.
useCases: A gardening or farming interaction where tilting pours.
A VR build where a hand grip rotates the can directly.
Any pouring or aiming action driven by rotation rather than a button.

params.tuning: Both where water comes from and the transform whose tilt is measured. Parent it correctly or pouring reads from the wrong axis.
Degrees from the spout's OWN starting orientation, not from world up — which is why the can can start at any angle.
Sample points along the stream, used for both drawing and for detecting plants. Too few and the stream can step over a small plant.
Roughly the stream's thickness. Together with arcResolution this decides what counts as watered.
Purely cosmetic curve on the stream, but it also moves the sample points, so it changes what gets watered.

gotchas.title: Tilt is relative to where the spout started
gotchas.body: Reparenting or re-orienting the can at runtime changes the reference. Start it in its resting pose.

gotchas.title: Watering is sample-point based, not a physical stream
gotchas.body: Plants are found by checking a radius around each sample. A plant between two samples with a small hit radius is missed.
